name: New Delhi (Delhi)
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching New Delhi: government-facing counterparty checks, Delhi High Court support and NCR real estate research.
eyebrow: National Capital Territory of Delhi, India
hero_lede: Delhi is India's seat of government and a services economy where ministries, regulators, public sector enterprises and corporate headquarters meet. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the capital, working from public records and coordinating qualified local professionals and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Delhi, the National Capital Territory that contains New Delhi, is the seat of India's Union Government, Parliament and Supreme Court, and the core of the wider National Capital Region. Its economy is overwhelmingly service-based: the Economic Survey of Delhi 2025-26 projects gross state domestic product of about Rs 13.27 lakh crore at current prices, growth of 9.42 per cent and services at 86.32 per cent of gross state value added, with manufacturing at 12.88 per cent. Per capita income is estimated at Rs 5.31 lakh, about two and a half times the national average. Government, trade, finance, real estate, hospitality and professional services dominate, and Delhi ranked sixth in the world for foreign tourist arrivals in 2024.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Delhi because so much of India's regulatory and procurement activity is decided there. Foreign companies bidding for public contracts, licences or approvals deal with ministries, public sector undertakings and intermediaries based in the capital, and need to know whether agents, consultants and joint venture partners carry corruption, conflict-of-interest or reputational risk. The region's large real estate market involves layered ownership and long-running title disputes. The Delhi High Court is a principal forum for commercial, intellectual property and arbitration-related litigation, so many cross-border disputes require evidence gathered in Delhi.

matters.title: Government-facing agent and consultant checks
matters.text: Foreign companies pursuing contracts or approvals in Delhi often rely on consultants, liaison agents and distributors. We examine ownership, directors, related parties, political and official connections disclosed in public sources, litigation and media to identify anti-corruption red flags before appointment or renewal.

matters.title: Joint venture and acquisition diligence
matters.text: Delhi-based groups frequently operate through networks of private companies held by family members. We map these structures from corporate filings, charges, litigation and media to show who controls the business, which related entities transact with it, and what disputes or enforcement histories exist.

matters.title: NCR real estate and title research
matters.text: Property in Delhi and the surrounding National Capital Region is affected by layered ownership, developer insolvency and title litigation. We review company records, court cases, insolvency proceedings and public notices to identify the parties behind projects and the disputes that may affect a transaction.

matters.title: Delhi High Court litigation support
matters.text: Commercial, intellectual property and arbitration-related disputes are often heard in the Delhi High Court. We support counsel with witness and party backgrounds, corporate histories, asset indicators and document trail reconstruction, scoped to the court's procedures and Indian evidence requirements.

matters.title: Counterfeit and brand protection matters
matters.text: Brand owners frequently bring infringement actions in Delhi against counterfeit and grey-market traders in the capital's wholesale markets. With local counsel, we research the businesses and people behind infringing activity, their corporate links and prior litigation, so that enforcement is properly targeted.

local_context.title: Delhi High Court
local_context.text: The Delhi High Court is unusual among Indian high courts in exercising original civil jurisdiction over higher-value suits, and it has had a Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division since the 2015 commercial courts reforms. It is a leading forum for intellectual property cases, petitions under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and company-related disputes. District commercial courts in Delhi hear lower-value commercial suits. The Supreme Court of India also sits in New Delhi.

local_context.title: Arbitration centres in Delhi
local_context.text: Delhi hosts two notable arbitral institutions. The Delhi International Arbitration Centre operates under the aegis of the Delhi High Court and administers a large volume of domestic commercial arbitrations. The New Delhi International Arbitration Centre, now the India International Arbitration Centre, was established under an Act of Parliament of 2019 as an institution of national importance to provide institutional arbitration, empanel arbitrators and train practitioners.

local_context.title: Company records and registries
local_context.text: Companies registered in Delhi fall under the Registrar of Companies for the National Capital Territory of Delhi and Haryana, and their filings are accessed through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal. Land and property documents are registered at sub-registrar offices across Delhi's districts, and records are not consolidated in a single searchable public database, so title research usually requires local counsel and searches at the relevant office.

local_context.title: Regulatory and enforcement bodies
local_context.text: Because Delhi is the national capital, the headquarters of central investigative and enforcement bodies, including the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate, are located there, as are the Central Vigilance Commission and most Union ministries. Delhi Police has an Economic Offences Wing for fraud complaints. Public procurement by ministries and central public sector enterprises generates many of the anti-corruption questions clients ask about Delhi counterparties.

local_context.title: No local investigator licensing
local_context.text: We have not identified a Delhi-specific statute licensing private detectives, consistent with the absence of a national licensing law. Lawful practice is shaped instead by general criminal law, data protection obligations and restrictions on accessing official records. TDSC therefore works through reputable local professionals and Indian counsel and does not use pretexting or obtain records that are not lawfully available.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Delhi and works on Delhi matters from Nashville. We start with the client's purpose and counsel's advice, whether a government-facing appointment, a joint venture, a Delhi High Court suit, an arbitration or a brand enforcement programme, and scope the research to it. Sources include Ministry of Corporate Affairs filings, court and arbitration records, insolvency and regulatory notices, and Hindi and English media. Where local enquiries or record searches are needed, we coordinate qualified Delhi professionals working under Indian counsel's direction, with attention to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Findings on official connections are reported with sources and confidence levels, never as allegations beyond what the evidence supports.

faqs.q: Are private investigators licensed in Delhi?
faqs.a: We have not identified a Delhi or national statute that licenses private detectives. That does not make every method lawful: data protection, criminal law and restrictions on official records still apply. TDSC works with established local professionals under the direction of Indian counsel and does not use pretexting or obtain non-public government records.

faqs.q: Which court hears large commercial disputes in Delhi?
faqs.a: Higher-value commercial suits are commonly heard by the Commercial Division of the Delhi High Court, which exercises original civil jurisdiction, while district commercial courts handle lower-value cases. The High Court also hears many arbitration petitions and intellectual property actions. Counsel selects the forum; our research is tailored to that court's procedure.

faqs.q: Which arbitration institutions operate in Delhi?
faqs.a: The Delhi International Arbitration Centre, under the aegis of the Delhi High Court, administers many domestic commercial arbitrations. The India International Arbitration Centre, established in New Delhi by a 2019 Act of Parliament, offers institutional arbitration of national and international disputes. Parties may also choose ad hoc arbitration seated in Delhi.

faqs.q: How do you check a Delhi consultant for corruption risk?
faqs.a: We review the consultant's company filings, directors and shareholders, related companies, litigation, regulatory actions and media coverage, and look for publicly documented links to officials or public sector bodies. We also test claimed experience and fee structures for plausibility. Findings are reported with sources so compliance teams can decide on further steps.

faqs.q: Can property ownership in Delhi be verified from public records?
faqs.a: Only in part. Registered documents sit with sub-registrar offices by district and are not available in one searchable public database, so title work usually needs Indian counsel and in-person searches. We complement this with company, insolvency and litigation research to identify developers, owners and disputes connected to the property.
